not_tested: A real `npm install`/`pip install` against a REACHABLE network (this track's sandbox is always `--network none`, by design — every install attempt against a real registry is expected to fail at the network layer, which is exactly the 'network calls observed' signal the report captures; a genuinely reachable-network scenario is out of scope by construction, not merely untested).
judgment_calls: No tool-invocation protocol exists anywhere in this codebase for 'run this candidate tool against a typed prompt' (none of the D1 issues define one). `testPrompts` is therefore used only for its COUNT — raw prompt text is never passed into the sandbox container at all, because Docker's default log driver persists container stdout/stderr to disk on the HOST, which would risk raw prompt text landing in durable state and directly violate the track's no-raw-prompts rule. The install step is the one real, well-defined action a tool-install proposal performs, and is what the vetter actually observes.

Forbidden-path violations are detected via pre-seeded sentinel files with a known content hash, checked for a content/hash change (or disappearance) after the run — verified by hand to work under a ROOT container user (a permission-bit/chmod-000 approach was considered and rejected: root bypasses permission bits, so it would not have detected a root-run write).

Credential ACCESS attempts (reads, not writes) are counted by how many times a sentinel's marker text appears in the captured install output — a `cat`/read prints the sentinel's content, which the run script redirects into a log this module parses for a COUNT ONLY; the raw log content itself is discarded and never returned or persisted.

Teardown correctness (`docker kill` + `docker rm -f` in a `finally`, not relying on `--rm` alone) was verified BY HAND against this environment before being encoded: killing the `docker run` CLI client process (e.g. on a timeout) does NOT stop the container — `--rm` only fires on the CONTAINER's own exit, not its client's. An orphaned container was reproduced and confirmed to require explicit `docker kill`/`docker rm -f` to reap.

Install methods are a closed, explicit set (`npm install`, `pip install`, plus a TEST-ONLY `local-script` escape hatch never accepted by the production proposal validator in D1.3) — an unrecognised installMethod fails closed to `verdict: 'unknown'` rather than guessing at a shell invocation.

The live Docker tests use `node:22-alpine` (already present locally in this environment, confirmed via `docker images` before writing any code) specifically to avoid any image-pull network dependency in the test suite; `--pull never` is also passed on every real `docker run` so a missing image fails fast and deterministically rather than the vetting infrastructure itself silently reaching the internet.

The 'network calls observed' detection is a closed set of known DNS/connection-failure error signatures (`getaddrinfo`, `Could not resolve host`, `failed to connect`, `ENETUNREACH`, `ECONNREFUSED`) parsed out of captured install output under `--network none`; a network-capable ecosystem tool not covered by one of these signatures would under-report rather than over-report — ponytail: extend the signature list if a real generator surfaces one this misses.
